title: Committee of Supply – Head U (Prime Minister's Office)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head U (Prime Minister's Office)

sections.label: Smart Nation initiative vision
sections.summary: The Smart Nation initiative envisages Singapore as a leading digital economy and world-class city with a responsive Government.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The Smart Nation initiative envisages a future Singapore that is a leading economy powered by digital innovations and world-class city with the Government that gives our citizens the best home possible and responds to their different and changing needs.

sections.label: COVID-19 technology measures update
sections.summary: The speaker asks for updates on technology-based measures against COVID-19 and future crises, and on electronic vaccination certificates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: On this note, I would like to ask whether the Government could provide an update on what other technology-based measures that might be in place to boost our fight against COVID-19 and future crises such as this.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: As our population gradually gets vaccinated, if, how and when can we expect electronic vaccination certificate to be issued?

sections.label: National Digital Identity timeline
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the National Digital Identity initiative is on track for widespread adoption in 2022 and its timeline for cross-border use.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Hence, the earlier we are digitally ready, the better.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: This brings me to my second question to ask the Ministry whether the National Digital Identity (NDI) initiative is on track for widespread adoption in 2022 and what is the expected timeline for NDI to be enabled for cross-border travels and transactions?

sections.label: TraceTogether and official online channels
sections.summary: Official online channels protect against misinformation, and TraceTogether enables contact tracing that prevented community outbreaks and saved the healthcare system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: We could also stay informed with the myriad of official online channels, established to protect us from misinformation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: Then, there is the TraceTogether, which allows for the establishing of an efficient contact tracing network.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: This network has effectively prevented widespread community outbreaks and saved our healthcare system from being overwhelmed.

sections.label: Arrests for leaking COVID-19 information
sections.summary: A public servant was arrested for sharing a draft media statement, and a civil servant for leaking COVID-19 case numbers before announcement.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: First, a public servant was arrested for sharing a draft media statement on schools moving into full home-based learning to curb the spread of COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Later, a civil servant was arrested for leaking the COVID-19 case numbers before official announcement.

sections.label: Smart Nation launch and progress
sections.summary: The Smart Nation initiative was launched in 2014 by Prime Minister Lee, and the Minister is asked how the vision is being made real.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, in 24 November 2014, the Smart Nation initiative was launched by Prime Minister Lee.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: He said, I quote, "Our vision is for Singapore to be a Smart Nation – a nation where people live meaningful and fulfilled lives, enabled seamlessly by technology, offering exciting opportunities for all." Echoing this, Minister-in-charge of the Smart Nation Office said, and I quote, "How do we include everyone in the digital revolution?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: This is all about designing solutions for people, and not the other way round." Now, more than six years into our journey to make Singapore a Smart Nation, can the Minister share how we are making our vision of Smart Nation real and tangible for Singaporeans and Singapore?

sections.label: Digitalisation and less tech-savvy people
sections.summary: A gap in tech savviness, not aversion to tech, prompts a question on designing Smart Nation solutions for less tech-savvy people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: It was because of a gap in tech savviness but not an aversion to use in tech.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: So, in our process of digitalisation, are we going to make an effort to drive a Smart Nation and design solutions for our people who are less tech savvy.

sections.label: Smart Nation technology during pandemic
sections.summary: Over 12 months of the pandemic, Smart Nation digital technology made a difference through MOE's student learning space, TraceTogether token and the supply airline app.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As we battle the pandemic over the past 12 months, we have witnessed clearly how Smart Nation applied digital technology that has made a difference to our lives, such as MOE's student learning space which enabled home-based learning for all students; TraceTogether (TT) token, which reduced contact tracing from four days to 1.5 days and the supply airline app which manage the distribution of critical supplies, such as 90 million masks and more than 500,000 meals for Redeem SG.

sections.label: TraceTogether, SafeEntry, SupplyAlly, RedeemSG use
sections.summary: TraceTogether, SafeEntry, SupplyAlly and RedeemSG helped reduce close-contact identification and quarantine time and distributed TT tokens and masks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: TraceTogether, which now has 4.7 million people using it, SafeEntry – all these have helped to reduce the time needed to identify and quarantine close contacts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: SupplyAlly and RedeemSG have been used to distribute more than 2.9 million TT tokens and 19 million masks.

sections.label: Government transactions completed digitally
sections.summary: Ninety-five percent of Government transactions between citizens and businesses are completed digitally end-to-end, paperless, cashless and presence-less.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Ninety-five percent of Government's transactions between citizens and businesses are today completed digitally end-to-end – 95% done paperless, cashless and presence-less.

sections.label: IT systems cloud migration by 2023
sections.summary: Seventy percent of eligible IT systems will have migrated to the cloud by 2023 under the Digital Government Blueprint.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Seventy percent of our eligible IT systems will have migrated to the cloud by 2023 under the Digital Government Blueprint.

sections.label: SingPass national digital identity update
sections.summary: SingPass provides access to over 1,400 digital services by 340 agencies, and pilot projects with Australia and Shenzhen, China are being embarked on.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Ms Tin Pei Ling asked for an update on the national digital identity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: I am glad to report that SingPass now provides seamless and secure access to over 1,400 digital services by 340 agencies, including private sector organisations, like some banks and insurance companies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: It was one million users in March last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We will be looking to extend the benefits of our national digital identity platform and to enable easier access to e-services beyond our shores, and we are embarking on pilot projects with Australia and Shenzhen, China.

sections.label: App downloads and e-services
sections.summary: Over 250,000 people have downloaded the app and can access a personalised dashboard of more than 70 Government e-services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: More than 250,000 people have already downloaded the app, and they can access a personalised dashboard of services to more than 70 Government e-services.

sections.label: PayNow mobile user increase
sections.summary: PayNow mobile users have increased by 31% compared to a year ago.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Compared to a year ago, we have a 31% increase in PayNow mobile users.

sections.label: E-payments receptiveness and digitally savvy
sections.summary: MAS is asked for an update on residents' receptiveness to e-payments and steps to ensure the less digitally savvy are not left behind.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: So, clearly, there is anxiety and people like to still handle cash and there is also anxiety about security.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: So, I would like MAS to give us an update on whether Singapore residents have been more receptive to e-payments in the past year, albeit that COVID-19 would have driven some of that.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: But what steps has MAS taken to ensure that the less digitally savvy amongst us are not left behind?

sections.label: MAS identity verification consultation
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes MAS's recent consultation paper on a proposed notice on identity verification, noting banks may have varying transactional security requirements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It does seem that different banks may have varying requirements when it comes to transactional security.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Therefore, I welcome the recent consultation paper by the MAS on a proposed notice on identity verification.

sections.label: MAS consideration and implementation
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MAS has considered this and whether it could be implemented.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Has the MAS considered this and could it be implemented?

sections.label: Insurance premium moratorium ending
sections.summary: MAS's six-month moratorium on insurance premium payments ends by 31 March 2021, and more residents may be unable to pay premiums.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the support given by MAS through the six-month moratorium on the payment of insurance premiums has been helpful, but it will end by 31 March 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We are likely to see more residents not being able to continue to pay their insurance premiums as the economy will not recover so quickly, including the unevenness of growth expected to continue across economic sectors.

sections.label: SGX sustainability reporting policy
sections.summary: MAS-regulated Singapore Stock Exchange has a comply-and-explain policy on sustainability reporting for listed companies, first announced in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the MAS-regulated Singapore Stock Exchange currently has a "comply and explain" policy on sustainability reporting for its listed companies, which was first announced in 2016.

sections.label: Move to mandatory regime
sections.summary: A suggestion is made to move from comply-and-explain to a mandatory regime, as some other major exchanges have done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Perhaps we could move from a "comply and explain" to a mandatory regime, as some other major exchanges have done.

sections.label: Policies surrendered in 2020
sections.summary: In 2020, despite recession, policies surrendered hit a five-year low of 153,000, or 0.9% of total in-force policies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In 2020, despite the economic recession, the number of policies surrendered hit a five-year low of 153,000, representing 0.9% of total in-force policies.

sections.label: PayNow registrations and transactions
sections.summary: PayNow registrations rose by 1.6 million last year to 4.9 million, with 80% of residents and businesses on PayNow.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Registrations for PayNow, for example, rose by 1.6 million last year, bringing the total number of registrations to 4.9 million.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This means that 80% of residents and businesses are now on PayNow.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This has driven PayNow transaction volumes to over $5 billion for the month of December 2020, which is double the volume a year ago.

sections.label: Cheque and ATM cash ratios
sections.summary: Cheque volumes relative to e-payments fell from 32% in 2016 to 12% last year, and ATM cash withdrawal ratios also fell.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The ratio of cheque volumes relative to e-payment volumes has dropped from 32% in 2016 to 18% in 2019 and then 12% last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Similarly, the ratio of ATM cash withdrawals to e-payments has also been falling, from 47% in 2016 to 24% in 2019, to then 17% last year.

sections.label: Number of touchpoints
sections.summary: There are now 4,100 of these touchpoints, compared to about 3,700 five years ago.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Today, there are 4,100 of these touchpoints, compared to about 3,700 five years ago.

sections.label: SGX ESG disclosure requirement
sections.summary: Since 2016, SGX RegCo has required SGX-listed companies to disclose material ESG risks and opportunities that could influence investors' decisions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Since 2016, Singapore Exchange Regulation (SGX RegCo) has required SGX-listed companies to disclose material environmental, social and governance (ESG) risks and opportunities that could influence the decisions of investors.

sections.label: SGX RegCo sustainability reporting consultation
sections.summary: SGX RegCo will consult this year on enhancements to its sustainability reporting requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: SGX RegCo will be consulting this year on enhancements to its sustainability reporting requirements.

sections.label: Mobilising capital into green economy
sections.summary: Mobilising capital into the green economy can create a virtuous cycle of growth, jobs and sustainable opportunities, requiring work on risk resilience, disclosures, green finance and technology.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: If we can successfully mobilise capital and new investment into the green economy, we can bring about a virtuous cycle of economic growth, creation of jobs and opportunities that are environmentally sustainable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In the coming years, we will need to work very hard with the industry and all our partners, to build environmental risk resilience into the financial system, of which, quality disclosures play an important part; expand green finance solutions and markets; and leverage innovation and technology.

sections.label: Singapore resident total fertility rate
sections.summary: The total fertility rate for resident Singaporeans stands at 1.14 as at 2019, the lowest registered in Singapore so far.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The TFR for resident Singaporeans stands at 1.14 as at 2019, the lowest registered in Singapore so far.

sections.label: South Korea spending on cash schemes
sections.summary: Since 2006, South Korea was reported to have spent almost US$250 billion on mostly cash schemes such as medical subsidies and baby cash.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Since 2006, South Korea was reported to have spent almost US$250 billion on mostly cash schemes such as medical subsidies for pregnant ladies, cash for each baby born and for raising the child till he was one, and monthly allowance for families with children under seven.

sections.label: Infant care and fertility support measures
sections.summary: The passage proposes free universal infant and child care up to age seven, and greater fertility care, education and techniques such as egg freezing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Consider providing free universal infant care and child care up to the age of seven.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: And next, for couples who are willing and unable or find difficulty in conceiving: one, provide a greater range of support measures of fertility care and education; two, study carefully and consider addition of new fertility techniques such as egg freezing into the slew of assisted reproduction measures.

sections.label: Singapore Total Fertility Rate
sections.summary: Singapore's Total Fertility Rate stands at 1.14 births.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Singapore’s Total Fertility Rate (TFR) is at a dismal 1.14 births.

sections.label: Childcare sick leave question
sections.summary: A question asks whether the PMO will consider specific childcare sick leave provided per child.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will PMO consider having specific childcare sick leave and providing this on a per child basis?

sections.label: Marriage rates age rise
sections.summary: Department of Statistics data show the highest marriage rates for males and females rose to ages 30 to 34 in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Based on the Department of Statistics data, the highest marriage rates among males and females in Singapore has grown to 30 to 34 years old in 2019, an increase of about five years from a decade ago.

sections.label: ART age limit removal
sections.summary: The Government removed the 45-year age limit for women undergoing ART and the cap on IVF cycles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Government's move from last year to remove the age limit of 45 years old for women undergoing ART procedures, as well as the cap on the number of IVF cycles a woman can undergo will certainly help sub-fertile couples.

sections.label: Mandating 50-50 childbirth leave
sections.summary: The proposal is to mandate 50-50 sharing of the current childbirth leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My proposal is to mandate the 50-50 sharing of the current childbirth leave.

sections.label: Mandating shared paternity leave
sections.summary: The Government can mandate splitting four months of leave half and half between mother and father, with subsidised employers and possible tax reliefs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To ensure higher usage of paternity leave, the Government can mandate that the four months be split half and half between mom and dad, with each of the employers getting subsidised for one month by the Government.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Mandating paternity leave by law, and making the one month of Government subsidy only available to both firms respectively if fathers fully utilise their paternity leave, will also compel companies to be supportive of their employees taking leave in the months post-birth.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To sweeten the deal for fathers, I would like to venture that the Government may want to also offer fathers income tax reliefs which are currently given to mothers, if paternity leave is fully utilised.

sections.label: Corruption case with extraterritorial effect
sections.summary: A brother and sister received near-maximum five-year jail terms for conspiring to secure China tenders and taking over $2 million in bribes, with part of the offence committed outside Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: An equally significant case came to light this year when a brother and sister were handed jail terms close to the maximum five years for conspiring to secure tenders for two companies in China and receiving in excess of $2 million in bribes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The case was significant because a substantive part of the offence was committed outside Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But because the Prevention of Corruption Act applies and has extraterritorial effect, the message was a clear one.

sections.label: FAS matter and corruption penalties
sections.summary: A Member asks when the FAS matter will close and calls for amending the Prevention of Corruption Act to raise penalties, noting Singapore ranked third least corrupt in TI's 2020 CPI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Separately, when can the public anticipate a closure to the FAS matter?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And finally, I call on the Government to amend the Prevention of Corruption Act to raise the penalties for corruption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Transparency International (TI) Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) 2020 ranked our country as being the third least corrupt country in the world.

sections.label: CPIB charging of three former employees
sections.summary: CPIB charged three former employees for bribery involving about $200 million, which the Member says shows the need to review PCA punishment provisions as an effective deterrent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Three days ago, CPIB issued a press statement highlighting the charging of three former employees for bribery in which the value of the subject is about $200 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It seems to me that this case is a timely reminder of the need to review the PCA provisions to ensure that the punishment provisions serve as an effective deterrent.

sections.label: SGUnited Jobs and Skills progress
sections.summary: A question asks about the progress of the public sector's SGUnited Jobs and Skills effort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: How has been the progress in the public sector's SGUnited Jobs and Skills effort?

sections.label: Marriage and parenthood support measures
sections.summary: COVID-19 led to about 10% fewer marriages in 2020 than 2019, so wedding reception and solemnisation capacity was raised to 100 and a $3,000 Baby Support Grant was introduced in October.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: COVID-19 has caused some Singaporeans to postpone their marriage, resulting in about 10% fewer marriages in 2020 compared to 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Because we recognised the importance of marriage and parenthood as a life-goal for Singaporeans, we prioritised these even as we tackled the health and economic consequences of COVID-19: We increased the attendance capacity for wedding receptions and solemnisations to 100, so couples can celebrate with more loved ones.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We introduced the $3,000 Baby Support Grant, or BSG, in October for Singaporean couples who have a child in these two years.

sections.label: Total fertility rate historic low
sections.summary: In 2020, Singapore's total fertility rate was 1.10, a historic low.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In 2020, our TFR was 1.10, which is a historic low.

sections.label: Housing grants and income ceiling
sections.summary: The qualifying income ceiling for subsidised housing rose to $14,000, and resale flat buyers can now receive up to $160,000 in grants.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We raised the qualifying income ceiling for subsidised housing from $12,000 to $14,000 in September 2019 so that more couples could have affordable housing options.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Those buying resale flats, can now receive up to $160,000 in housing grants, up from $90,000 five years ago.

sections.label: Second child CDA co-matching
sections.summary: Government co-matching for the second child's Child Development Account doubles to $6,000, raising maximum total contributions to $9,000 for eligible SC children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We reviewed this and will provide more support for couples having their second child.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We will double the maximum dollar-for-dollar Government co-matching of parents' savings in the Child Development Account (CDA) for the second child, from $3,000 to $6,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: With this enhancement, the maximum total Government contributions for the second child's CDA will increase from $6,000 to $9,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: All Singapore Citizen, or SC, children who are the second child, and whose date of birth or estimated date of delivery is on or after 1 January 2021, will be eligible.

sections.label: Paternity and adoption benefits
sections.summary: The Government-Paid Paternity Benefit and Government-Paid Adoption Benefit will be introduced to support this group of parents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To better support this group of parents, we will introduce the Government-Paid Paternity Benefit (GPPB) and Government-Paid Adoption Benefit (GPAB).

sections.label: New citizens and PRs in 2020
sections.summary: About 21,100 new citizens and 27,500 new Permanent Residents were granted in 2020, lower than previous years due to COVID-19 restrictions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In 2020, we granted about 21,100 new citizens, and 27,500 new Permanent Residents (PRs).

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: These figures are lower than previous years due to travel restrictions and operational issues arising from COVID-19.

sections.label: LTVP for foreign spouses
sections.summary: Widowed or divorced foreign spouses with custody of minor Singaporean children will generally be allowed to stay on a Long-term Visit Pass until the child becomes an adult.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Widowed or divorced foreign spouses, with custody of minor Singaporean children, will generally be allowed to stay here on a Long-term Visit Pass (LTVP) until the child becomes an adult.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: While it is not possible to guarantee PR or citizenship to any foreigner, foreign spouses are generally considered more favourably, especially when they have Singaporean children.

sections.label: Singapore corruption rankings and reports
sections.summary: Singapore ranked fourth in the 2019 Corruption Perceptions Index and topped the 2020 Political and Economic Risk Consultancy survey, with 350 corruption-related reports in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This indicates that the Transparency International Corruption Perceptions Index for 2019 ranked Singapore fourth out of 180 countries and territories with a high score of 85.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: And in the latest Political and Economic Risk Consultancy 2020 corruption survey, Singapore maintained top position and improved its score to 1.73 as compared to a score of 1.85 the previous year, zero being the best score.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In 2019, CPIB received 350 corruption-related reports compared to 358 in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: And in 2019, the percentage of corruption-related reports registered for investigation increased to 34% compared to the annual average of 28% over the preceding four years, but generally speaking, we are doing well on that front and the cases have been prosecuted with all due dispatch.

sections.label: MLA request to Brazil
sections.summary: AGC and CPIB sent a mutual legal assistance request to Brazil to obtain information from overseas witnesses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: As there is a need to obtain additional information from other witnesses based overseas, AGC and CPIB have worked together to send a mutual legal assistance, MLA request to Brazil following the earlier fact-finding trips.

sections.label: CPIB review of Act
sections.summary: CPIB is reviewing the Act with AGC, covering provisions including disgorgement of corrupt benefits and informer identity protection.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The review of this Act by CPIB is underway.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: CPIB has been working in consultation with AGC on a comprehensive list of provisions for the review, some of which included the disgorgement of corrupt benefits from perpetrators and strengthening the protection of informers' identity.

sections.label: Public Service retirement ages raised
sections.summary: The Public Service placed 21,000 local workers and will raise retirement and re-employment ages to 63 and 68 from 1 July 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Mr Patrick Tay asked how the Public Service has helped Singaporeans impacted by the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We have worked with unions and other partners to place some 21,000 local workers so far in short-term and long-term jobs and traineeships across the public sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: But we are clear that in the longer term, with an ageing and shrinking local workforce, we must help our people work longer with new capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Therefore, the Public Service will raise its retirement and re-employment ages to 63 and 68 respectively from 1 July 2021, one year ahead of the national schedule, as earlier committed.

sections.label: Childcare leave employability questions
sections.summary: The Member asked whether studies show childcare leave decreases employability and whether PMO can study childcare sick leave usage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: But I think we need to remember that the essential workers cannot work from home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: So, could I ask, one, whether the Minister is aware of any studies in Singapore that show that by increasing childcare leave, it would decrease the employability of a person?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Two, could I ask whether PMO can study the usage of childcare sick leave amongst our public servants, and then use this study to decide on whether to extend it to everyone else?

sections.label: Long-term visit pass until 21
sections.summary: The Member sought clarification that widowed or abandoned spouses get long-term visit pass only until the Singaporean child is 21.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Minister mentioned just now, and I wanted to seek clarification, that these spouses who are widowed or abandoned, the Minister mentioned that they would only get long-term visit pass until the Singaporean child is 21.

sections.label: ICA case-by-case family ties
sections.summary: ICA considers each case on its own merits, and family ties will mean greater priority.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I was not making a statement as to a specific time when it is considered.

sentences.text: I think ICA considers each case on its own merits and the point I was making is that family ties will mean greater priority.
